subject: Error/Bug with modified pars in mint-model

messages.author: 1ec3f8d9a5847ab4
messages.subject: Error/Bug with modified pars in mint-model
parts:
Hi Phil,

I'm currently trying to fit a mirt model with predefined parameters in a MCAT-simulation with real data. When doing that for unidimensional models (one dimension at a time) everything works fine, but with my multidimensional model I get an error message I can't seem to solve. Could that one a bug or am I doing something wrong? Could you help me?

Background:
I calibrated a mirt-model for my MCAT simulation with some real personality data (6-point Likert-scale, model = "graded"). In the next step I want to simulate a MCAT with a different (also real) dataset in order to observe whether my calibrated MCAT works as expected with independent data. My calibration data was N > 20k and my confirmation dataset is N > 20k as well, without any missing values in either of it. My mirt model has 14 dimensions and includes all covariances (between-item multidimensionality). 

Here's my code:

load(file = calibration mirt-model)

coef <- coef(mirt.model)

model <- 'F1 = i7,i22,i37,i53,i69,i85,i100,i115,i130,i144,i159,i172,i196,i204
          F2 = i8,i23,i38,i54,i70,i86,i101,i116,i131,i145,i173,i186
          F3 = i9,i24,i39,i55,i71,i87,i102,i117,i132,i146,i160,i174,i187,i197,i205
          F4 = i11,i26,i41,i57,i73,i89,i104,i119,i134,i148,i162,i176,i188,i206
          F5 = i12,i27,i42,i58,i74,i90,i105,i120,i135,i149,i163,i177,i189,i198
          F6 = i13,i28,i43,i59,i75,i91,i106,i121,i136,i150,i164,i178,i190,i199
          F7 = i14,i29,i44,i60,i76,i92,i107,i122,i151,i165,i179,i191
          F8 = i2,i16,i31,i46,i62,i78,i94,i109,i124,i138,i153,i167,i181,i192,i201,i208
          F9 = i1,i15,i30,i45,i61,i77,i93,i108,i123,i137,i152,i166,i180,i200,i207
          F10 = i3,i17,i32,i47,i63,i79,i95,i110,i125,i139,i154,i168,i182
          F11 = i10,i25,i40,i56,i72,i88,i103,i118,i133,i147,i161,i175
          F12 = i4,i18,i33,i48,i64,i80,i96,i111,i126,i140,i155,i169,i183,i193,i202,i209
          F13 = i5,i19,i34,i49,i65,i81,i97,i112,i127,i141,i156,i170,i184
          F14 = i6,i20,i35,i50,i66,i82,i98,i113,i128,i142,i157,i171,i185,i194,i203,i210
          COV = F1*F2*F3*F4*F5*F6*F7*F8*F9*F10*F11*F12*F13*F14'

pars <- mirt(data = data, model = model, 'graded', SE = TRUE, pars = "values") 

pars$est <- FALSE 

# overwriting the pars object with the precalibrated parameters of the first mirt-model
for (item in items) { # items is a vector of all items used in the model
   pars$value[which(pars$item == item)] <- coef[[item]][1,]
}

pars$value[which(pars$item == "GROUP")] <- coef$GroupPars[1,] 

#using the pars object to fit a mirt model with "old" parameters on "new" data
mirt.model.confirmation <- mirt(data = data, model = model, itemtype = 'graded', pars = pars, method = "MHRM")


That always throws me this error message:

error in colMeans(do.call(rbind, aveAR)) :
  'x' must be an array of at least two dimensions 

(translated error message from german)


Do you have any clue? It's very important for my doctoral thesis to solve this, so I would be very thankful for your help!

Best wishes

Nick
